title: Task envelope
description: SPEC.md §6: the value of the `approval:` frontmatter key on a Backlog.md-style task file. This schema governs that value only — sibling board keys (id, title, status) belong to Backlog.md and are out of scope. A task with no envelope is valid markdown; it simply cannot request side-effecting execution (§6).

origin.description: SPEC.md §6.2: provenance of the task. MUST be present — an envelope with no traceable origin cannot be gated.

app.description: SPEC.md §6.2 `origin.app` (MUST): source system that created this task (`example-capture`, `manual`, …).

created_by.description: SPEC.md §6.2 `origin.created_by` (MUST): `human:<id>` or `agent:<id>`. A bare identifier with no principal-kind prefix is rejected.

route.description: SPEC.md §6.2: routing of the task. Routing proposals from agents are events, never silent edits to this block.

assignee.description: SPEC.md §6.2 `route.assignee` (SHOULD): the literal `human`, or `agent:<id>`. Note the asymmetry with `origin.created_by`: a human assignee is unqualified because the queue, not an id, is the destination.

rationale.description: SPEC.md §6.1: free-text justification for the routing decision, carried for audit and monitoring.

confidence.description: SPEC.md §6.2 `route.confidence` (MAY): 0.0–1.0 routing confidence, used as a monitoring signal (§11). Never a gate on its own.

state.description: SPEC.md §6.3: approval lifecycle state, distinct from the board `status`. A projection of the event log — the daemon writes it after the event is appended, never the reverse.

actions.description: SPEC.md §6.2 `actions[]`: declared side effects. MUST be present for execution; absent means the task cannot request an execution token (§7: a class MUST be declared before a token can be requested for it).

class.description: SPEC.md §7: dotted, hierarchical side-effect class (`communicate.email.external`, `financial.spend`). Lowercase dot-separated segments of [a-z0-9_-]; top-level namespaces are reserved by the spec, sub-classes are extensible.

summary.description: SPEC.md §6.2: one-line human-readable description of the effect, rendered into the approval request and the queue (§9).

reversible.description: SPEC.md §7: whether the effect can be undone. `false` actions MUST NOT be eligible for `autonomous` regardless of policy — the runtime enforces that floor.

est_cost_usd.description: SPEC.md §6.2: estimated cost in USD, checked against task and policy budgets (conjunctively).

idempotency_key.description: SPEC.md §6.2 (MUST per action): stable string; adapters MUST refuse to execute the same key twice.

payload_hash.description: SPEC.md §6.2 (amended: MUST for `manual` actions, SHOULD otherwise): SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 canonical serialization of the action's concrete payload — for a message send, the full body and recipients; for `approval run`, the argv array and cwd; for a record write, the proposed record content. The payload itself is stored or referenced by the request so channels can display it; the hash is what approval binds to (§10). Optional here because this schema cannot know an action's resolved autonomy — the MUST for `manual` is enforced at request time by the gate, which refuses `payload-hash-required`.

budget.description: SPEC.md §6.2 `budget` (MAY): task-level caps, conjunctive with policy budgets — the stricter of the two binds.

max_cost_usd.description: SPEC.md §6.2: maximum total spend in USD across this task's actions.

max_latency.description: SPEC.md §6.1: duration string bounding how long the request may stay pending (`6h`, `30m`, `7d`). Integer magnitude plus one unit suffix.
